# MCP Discord Bot Server

Inspect a Discord application bot and the servers it has joined from a local MCP client.

[![AceDataCloud/DiscordBotMCP MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/AceDataCloud/DiscordBotMCP/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/AceDataCloud/DiscordBotMCP)

## Connect a Discord application bot

Create a bot in the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and install it in the server you want to inspect. Supply the application's bot token to the local MCP process through `DISCORDBOT_TOKEN`. These tools use the [Discord REST API](https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference) with bot authentication and require no privileged gateway intents.

Configure the MCP client to run the following command over stdio. For example, with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed and `DISCORDBOT_TOKEN` set in the client's environment:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "discord-bot": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-discord-bot", "--bot-account"]
    }
  }
}
```

Call `discord_whoami` for the bot's ID and username. `discord_list_guilds` returns up to 200 server IDs and names. Pass the last ID as `after` to read another page.

## Existing proxy installations

Running `mcp-discord-bot` without `--bot-account` preserves the separate Discord Agent Proxy interface. That client uses the instance URL `DISCORD_BOT_BASE_URL` and its own proxy access token `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. The application bot mode uses only `DISCORDBOT_TOKEN` and connects directly to Discord. Discord [prohibits automation of personal accounts](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002192352-Automated-User-Accounts-Self-Bots).
